about: A PROJECT-DEFINED KANNADA B2 CONTENT INVENTORY, NOT AN EXTERNAL KANNADA QUALIFICATION. It bounds the content needed to realise this project's committed B2 four-skill task shape. The sources support a useful first inventory, but none supplies a finite Kannada B2 grammar or word list. Every dimension therefore remains partial, uncovered points remain visible work, and coverage must never be reported as exam readiness.
source: PROJECT-DEFINED synthesis of the Council of Europe CEFR Companion Volume (2020), CIIL's intermediate Kannada four-skill laboratory text, Unicode 18.0 section 12.8, official LDC-IL Kannada corpus-domain documentation, and the committed Coding Adventures Kannada B2 task shape. Each source is used only for the boundary it can support.

anchors.title: Council of Europe, CEFR Companion Volume (2020)
anchors.note: Supplies B2 reception, production, interaction, mediation, linguistic, sociolinguistic, and pragmatic descriptors. It defines a proficiency boundary, not Kannada exponents, and the Council of Europe does not certify this project assessment.

anchors.title: CIIL, Kannada madhyama prayogashala pathya
anchors.note: Provides an intermediate Kannada L2 four-skill instructional boundary across varied genres. It is a teaching text, not a finite B2 grammar, an examination syllabus, or evidence that this book covers its demands.

anchors.title: Unicode Standard 18.0, section 12.8 Kannada
anchors.note: Closes the encoding model for Kannada characters, virama, live and dead consonants, atomic vowels, and conjunct formation. It does not close spelling, punctuation, handwriting, pronunciation, or B2 processing demands.

anchors.title: LDC-IL Release Documentation
anchors.note: Documents contemporary Kannada corpus material across aesthetics, commerce, mass media, official documents, science and technology, and social sciences. Those are domain boundaries, not a B2 word list or frequency threshold.

anchors.title: Coding Adventures Kannada B2 four-skill task shape
anchors.note: Fixes the genres, input lengths, response modes, timing, interaction, and scoring demands that the content inventory must make executable. It defines how content is sampled, not which content has been taught.

communicative-functions.note: CEFR provides a generic B2 functional boundary and the task shape names the performances this project samples. Neither selects the Kannada exponents, discourse markers, repair moves, or register choices that realise those functions, so the dimension is not closed.

grammar.note: The CIIL source demonstrates intermediate four-skill Kannada instruction and CEFR describes B2 range and control, but neither is a finite Kannada B2 grammar. The points below are a reviewable project selection, not a finite Kannada B2 grammar.

phonology-orthography.note: Unicode closes the character and conjunct encoding model, while the other anchors establish four-skill use and the assessed writing demands. They do not close spelling, punctuation, handwriting, regional pronunciation, listening speed, or extended-text processing.

lexicon.note: LDC-IL establishes contemporary domains and the other anchors establish genre use, but a corpus domain list is not a B2 word list. No source here supplies a level-bounded lemma inventory, frequency threshold, productive collocation set, or regional-variant boundary.

probeSemantics: A point is covered only when every atom in its probe is introduced by a Kannada-track lesson. probe: null means the first source-bounded inventory has no exact lesson-atom mapping for that demand. A covered probe is evidence of named lesson coverage only; it is never evidence of task performance, mock readiness, B2 attainment, or external certification.

points.label: build a reasoned argument with an explicit position, linked reasons, evidence, and conclusion
points.note: The corpus has foundation atoms for position and cause-result linking, but they do not demonstrate evidence, conclusion, or a sustained B2 argument, so this complete demand remains unmapped.

points.label: follow and produce a reported feature that distinguishes source, fact, interpretation, and stance
points.note: The task shape requires reporting, but the current lesson atoms do not jointly name source attribution, fact-opinion distinction, and report organisation.

points.label: understand and give a detailed procedure with sequence, conditions, exceptions, and required actions
points.note: The corpus has sequencing and obligation foundations, but not an exact atom set for conditions, exceptions, required actions, and sustained procedural organisation, so the demand remains unmapped.

points.label: interpret literary or cultural prose for voice, figurative effect, cultural inference, and textual support
points.note: Aesthetics is a documented corpus domain, but domain presence neither enumerates interpretive language nor proves literary inference.

points.label: track a multiparty discussion by speaker, proposal, stance, agreement, disagreement, and outcome
points.note: The current corpus has no exact atom set for sustained speaker tracking and implicit interpersonal alignment.

points.label: solve a collaborative problem by proposing, comparing, evaluating, negotiating, and deciding
points.note: Comparison and real-condition foundations exist, but proposal, evaluation, turn management, tactful disagreement, repair, and negotiated closure do not have an exact complete probe.

points.label: write a formal interaction text that requests, responds, complains, proposes, or explains for a named audience
points.note: The assessment requires audience and register control, but the inventory cannot yet map a complete formal interaction-text repertoire to lesson atoms.

points.label: present a position, defend it under follow-up questions, qualify a claim, and reformulate after challenge
points.note: Opinion, reason, and counterfactual atoms are foundations only; no exact probe demonstrates four-minute organisation, defence under challenge, qualification, or responsive reformulation.

points.label: mediate complex information by selecting, relating, clarifying, and adapting it for another person
points.note: CEFR makes mediation explicit at B2, while the current Kannada atoms do not enumerate a dependable mediation repertoire.

points.label: link claim, reason, result, and conclusion with a varied causal and consequential repertoire
points.note: The corpus teaches an initial causal repertoire, but no exact atom set demonstrates varied linking through claim, reason, result, and conclusion with discourse-length accuracy and pragmatic choice.

points.label: express real, negative, and contingency-framed conditions across practical and argumentative contexts
points.note: The named conditional forms are taught foundations, but no exact atom set demonstrates their productive B2 range across practical and argumentative contexts or their register distribution.

points.label: frame unreal situations, consequences, qualifications, and alternative outcomes
points.note: The corpus teaches a compact unreal-condition foundation, not an exact atom set demonstrating situations, consequences, qualifications, alternatives, and the wider Kannada B2 counterfactual system.

points.label: express obligation, prohibition, recommendation, permission, and degrees of necessity
points.note: Obligation and prohibition are taught foundations, but recommendation, permission, mitigation, degrees of necessity, and register-sensitive force lack an exact complete probe.

points.label: organise extended time relations with sequence, anteriority, simultaneity, duration, and boundaries
points.note: Several time relations are taught foundations, but simultaneity and the full extended-text tense-aspect and discourse-time boundary lack an exact complete probe.

points.label: choose past, ongoing-past, and habitual-past framing in connected narrative and report
points.note: The forms are taught foundations, but no exact atom set establishes connected narrative and report control, aspectual nuance, or regional distribution.

points.label: compare entities, quantities, spans, and extremes while preserving the intended standard of comparison
points.note: Comparison and range forms are taught foundations, but no exact atom set demonstrates entity, quantity, span, extreme, standard-of-comparison, nuanced evaluation, and idiomatic selection together.

points.label: report speech, thought, evidence, and attributed claims with source and stance kept clear
points.note: No exact lesson-atom set currently closes direct and indirect reporting, evidential distance, source attribution, and stance.

points.label: control contemporary spoken, neutral written, and formal written Kannada without unmotivated register mixing
points.note: The sources establish register-sensitive use and varied domains, but no finite exponent list closes the spoken-written-formal boundary.

points.label: read and write the Kannada character inventory with dependent vowel signs attached to the correct base
points.note: Six recognition atoms establish only part of the script foundation; they do not demonstrate the whole character inventory, accurate extended handwriting, or B2 reading fluency.

points.label: resolve virama, dead and live consonants, and subscript ottakshara in unfamiliar words
points.note: Unicode closes the structural model and the corpus has recognition examples, but no exact probe demonstrates resolution and production in unfamiliar words.

points.label: use full stop, comma, question mark, colon, quotation marks, parentheses, and dash to organise extended text
points.note: The punctuation marks have recognition atoms, but no exact probe demonstrates their productive use to organise extended text.

points.label: spell inflected and derived forms while preserving visible morpheme boundaries and conventional forms
points.note: Unicode explains character composition, not Kannada spelling conventions across inflection, derivation, compounding, or sandhi.

points.label: read 1,800–2,300 words of multi-genre Kannada efficiently while retaining argument and detail
points.note: Lesson completion does not measure the sustained processing rate, comprehension, or fatigue boundary required by the reading paper.

points.label: understand connected Kannada at 150–170 words per minute after one orienting preview
points.note: A written inventory cannot infer listening-speed control from vocabulary atoms; this demand needs recorded input and performance evidence.

points.label: recognise documented regional Kannada voices without treating one accent as the only correct model
points.note: The task shape requires regional voices, but the current lesson metadata does not provide a reviewed regional listening inventory.

points.label: produce intelligible connected speech with stress, rhythm, phrasing, and repair that sustain extended interaction
points.note: Pronunciation and fluency are assessment criteria, but lesson-atom presence cannot demonstrate connected-speech performance.

points.label: handwrite 220–280 words legibly with rounded letterforms, stable vowel-sign placement, and subscript conjuncts
points.note: The encoding model cannot stand in for timed handwriting quality; a productive sample and trained scoring are required.

points.label: public institutions, official documents, civic processes, rights, obligations, and public services
points.note: Official documents establish a contemporary domain, not a level-bounded lemma, collocation, or formula inventory.

points.label: commerce, work, money, consumer decisions, proposals, complaints, and negotiated outcomes
points.note: Commerce is a corpus domain and negotiation is a task demand; neither source supplies the closed Kannada lexical set.

points.label: mass media, reporting, source attribution, public debate, evidence, and audience response
points.note: Mass media bounds a source domain, but reporting verbs, source formulas, stance collocations, and genre conventions remain unclosed.

points.label: science and technology, processes, measurements, cause and effect, uncertainty, and practical consequences
points.note: Science and technology is a measured LDC-IL domain, not a B2 vocabulary threshold or a productive collocation list.

points.label: social sciences, education, community change, comparison, trends, causes, and consequences
points.note: The domain is sourced, but the current inventory cannot close terminology, evaluative language, trend language, or register.

points.label: health, symptoms, treatment, risk, advice, and informed decisions in extended explanation
points.note: The corpus has one medicine atom, which cannot demonstrate this health-domain repertoire; one example word never proves a lexical domain, so the point remains unmapped.

points.label: environment, agriculture, place, resources, change, competing priorities, and practical responses
points.note: Contemporary-domain evidence motivates the point, but no primary source here supplies a finite B2 environmental lexicon.

points.label: aesthetics, music, literature, cultural practice, interpretation, evaluation, and personal response
points.note: The corpus has one music atom, which cannot demonstrate this aesthetics-domain repertoire; one example word never proves a lexical domain, so the point remains unmapped.

points.label: cross-domain academic and public-language repertoire: stance, evidence, qualification, cohesion, reformulation, and summary
points.note: This cross-domain repertoire makes the genres executable, but the sources do not yield a finite Kannada B2 list of general-purpose lemmas and collocations.
